title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 50
paragraphs: In consequence of this accusation, Cleomenes son of Anaxandrides, king of the Spartans, crossed over to Aegina intending to seize the Aeginetans most guilty in the matter. But as he was trying to seize them, certain of the Aeginetans opposed him, and among them especially Crius son of Polycritus, who said that Cleomenes should not carry off a single Aeginetan with impunity, for he was doing this (he said) without the authority of the Spartan state, having been persuaded to it by the Athenians with money; otherwise he would have come and seized them in company with the other king. He said this because of a message received from Demaratus. Then Cleomenes, as he was leaving Aegina, asked Crius what his name was, and he told him the truth; and Cleomenes said to him: “Now then, Ram, bind your horns with bronze, for you will have a great trouble to contend with shortly.” (The Greek word krios also means “ram.”)
